paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The line plot compares the loss values of two models—Vanilla Transformer and SepLLM—across increasing computational cost measured in TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations). The x-axis, labeled “TFLOPs,” ranges from 0.00 to 1.25×10⁹ with major tick marks at intervals of 0.25×10⁹. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” spans from 2.40 to 2.75, with major gridlines every 0.05 units. The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with downward-pointing triangle markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.77 loss at 0 TFLOPs and gradually declines to about 2.50 loss near 1.2×10⁹ TFLOPs. The “SepLLM” model is shown with a red line and circular markers, also solid; it starts at roughly 2.75 loss and drops more steeply, reaching approximately 2.48 loss at 1.2×10⁹ TFLOPs. A green dashed horizontal line at Loss = 2.50 highlights a reference point, and a green bracket labeled “1.28×” spans from ~1.0×10⁹ to ~1.25×10⁹ TFLOPs, indicating the computational efficiency gain of SepLLM over Vanilla at that loss level. Both lines exhibit a consistent downward trend, with SepLLM consistently achieving lower loss than Vanilla across the entire TFLOP range.
